content.thinking:
Found the bug! The final drain marks jobs "applied" but does NOT update `slot_last_applied` (and `slot_cached`). Per the spec: "After the final packet, finish every remaining job in (done,id) order by the same completion rules." — the same completion rules include updating the occupant's cached class and last applied ID. So a job applied during the drain must update last_applied, affecting subsequent drain statuses (superseded).

Let me fix: add `slot_cached[s] = job[10]` and `slot_last_applied[s] = jid` in the drain's applied branch.

Note: cached class updates during the drain don't affect any output (no more packets), but last_applied does affect subsequent statuses. Both must be updated for correctness of subsequent statuses.

Let me fix this and re-run all tests.

content.text: Found the bug: the final drain marks jobs "applied" but doesn't update the slot's `last_applied`/`cached`, so later drain jobs aren't correctly marked "superseded". Fixing:

arguments.command:
cd /app && python3 - << 'PYEOF'
src = open('submission/main.py').read()
old = '''    # ---- final drain ----
    while pending:
        (done, jid) = heappop_(pending)
        job = jobs[jid]
        s = job[3]
        if slot_occ[s] != job[2] or slot_gen[s] != job[4]:
            job[11] = "stale"
        elif jid <= slot_last_applied[s]:
            job[11] = "superseded"
        else:
            job[11] = "applied"
'''
new = '''    # ---- final drain (same completion rules, no expiry / refill) ----
    while pending:
        (done, jid) = heappop_(pending)
        job = jobs[jid]
        s = job[3]
        if slot_occ[s] != job[2] or slot_gen[s] != job[4]:
            job[11] = "stale"
        elif jid <= slot_last_applied[s]:
            job[11] = "superseded"
        else:
            job[11] = "applied"
            slot_cached[s] = job[10]
            slot_last_applied[s] = jid
'''
assert old in src
open('submission/main.py','w').write(src.replace(old, new))
print("patched")
PYEOF
cd /app && python3 submission/main.py < examples/input.json | python3 -c "
